content:
The late Princess Diana's younger brother, Charles Spencer, has claimed in his new book that King Charles said she would be quickly forgotten after the tragic death in 1997. The claims come from reports about Spencer's upcoming memoir.

According to extracts from the new book "Shadows of a Swan: My Sister, Diana," published by the Daily Mail on Wednesday, Spencer claimed he had a heated phone argument with the current King over whether Princes William and Harry should walk behind their mother's coffin in the funeral procession.

In the new book, due to be published next week, Spencer wrote: "Prince Charles continued to vent his anger at length, I did not interrupt him, and then he stopped."

He continued: "I thought the silence meant he was trying to control his emotions, but then he burst out over the phone with all the resentment he had harboured towards Diana, and his fear that the whole world was so shocked by her death. 'Don't worry,' he said through gritted teeth, 'we will forget her in no time!'"

Spencer wrote that he was utterly taken aback by the remarks and it took him a few seconds to recover.

He wrote: "I said in a flat voice: 'I cannot believe you just said that.' And then I hung up."

The Daily Mail reported on Tuesday that four copies of Spencer's new book were stolen in the Netherlands, with thieves taking them from a van, and Dutch authorities are investigating the burglary.

A publishing industry source described the incident as "highly suspicious," telling the paper: "Nothing like this has ever happened before."

They told the Daily Mail: "This book is likely to be the most important publication of the year, and the authorities have always maintained extremely tight security over it."

Spencer's spokesperson did not immediately respond to HuffPost's inquiry.

A Buckingham Palace spokesperson, responding to HuffPost's inquiry, said: "It is our policy as a rule not to comment on the contents of books, but His Majesty is mindful that grief, in time, can cloud rational thought and judgment, and colour memory in ways that are not readily apparent to others—even after many years."

Spencer delivered a speech at Diana's funeral at Westminster Abbey, speaking passionately to denounce the British tabloids' relentless pursuit of her, describing her as "the most hunted person of the modern age."

Spencer recently posted on social media, saying the upcoming new book is "the most personal of the ten books I have written over the past thirty years."

He wrote: "Ultimately, this is a brother offering the simplest tribute to an extraordinary sister."

Carly Ledbetter contributed to this report.
